rows.description: An adult crouches, gives one simple instruction and waits, and the child listens. Short, concrete statements and a calm voice work better than long explanations.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A parent tells a child in simple terms why a relative is ill or the family is moving. Honesty at the child's level builds trust, while secrecy breeds imagined worse stories.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: A child hears why can't you be like your cousin and is left feeling inadequate. Children often take sarcasm literally and carry comparison into their self-image for years.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: insecurity

rows.description: A teenager addressed like a small child by a teacher or a relative feels disrespected and turns defiant. Treating them as a developing adult with real opinions draws cooperation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, hostility

rows.description: A young adult who hears a child describe a fear or a drawing asks what it is about before judging. Curious attention gives children words and trust to bring bigger worries later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: fear, anxiety, curiosity, trust

rows.description: A child stays quiet and avoids eye contact when a teacher asks a question, fearing scolding. Fear of authority can make children hide confusion, and warmth from the teacher opens them up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, fear, confusion

rows.description: A teenager who argues with a principal or a parent may be seeking fairness or simply testing power. Respectful directness such as may I explain, works better than rudeness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, hostility

rows.description: A student emailing a professor or asking a manager for feedback worries about seeming needy. Clear, brief, specific requests come across as engaged, not weak.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, interest

rows.description: A young employee tells a manager I see it differently, and here is the risk, offers data and a solution, and accepts the decision afterwards. Disagreeing with respect and commitment builds trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, trust

rows.description: A person shouted at or belittled by a superior may freeze and doubt themselves. Documenting incidents, seeking allies and knowing formal channels protects, since submission does not fix abuse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: doubt
